text:
alex_w: Hey team — staging terraform apply failed and left a lock. CI job 4321 exited but the lock didn't clear. Anyone have bandwidth to check? Error snippet below.

deploy-bot: CI job 4321: apply aborted (exit 1). terraform: Error locking state: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed

maria_dev: Which lock table is that against? Staging uses `redwood-terraform-staging-locks` (DynamoDB). Can someone paste the LockID from the error?

jamal: I saw an apply start from gitlab-runner-7 earlier. Could be a stuck runner. You can list locks quickly:
```
aws dynamodb scan --table-name redwood-terraform-staging-locks --region us-west-2
```

maria_dev: If the LockID looks like `ci-4321` you can inspect the item:
```
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name redwood-terraform-staging-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"ci-4321"}}' --region us-west-2
```
And if there's no active terraform process, you can run (from the same workspace):
```
terraform force-unlock ci-4321
```
(only do that after confirming no live process)

alex_w: Pasted the error log from the runner: 
```
Error: Error locking state: Error acquiring the state lock: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed
Lock Info: {"ID":"ci-4321","Who":"gitlab-runner-7","Operation":"Apply","Created":"2026-03-16T21:05:12Z"}
```

maria_dev: Another thing — sometimes refresh causes long waits if a resource was changed manually. You can run a plan skipping refresh, then import the resource and reconcile:
```
terraform plan -refresh=false -target=module.db.aws_db_subnet_group.main
terraform import module.db.aws_db_subnet_group.main subnet-0a1b2c3d
```
This avoids a long blocking refresh while you sort the state.

infra-ops: I checked the runner and there's no active terraform process. I ran `terraform force-unlock ci-4321` from an ops host (same workspace) and retriggered the CI apply. The apply progressed past the refresh step. We discovered `aws_db_subnet_group.main` was being replaced because someone edited the subnet group in the console — drift. I re-imported the existing subnet group, adjusted the TF config to match the actual subnets, and then re-ran plan/apply. Clean now.

sre-bot: Lock `ci-4321` force-unlocked by infra-ops at 2026-03-16T21:42:03Z :unlock: 

jamal: Filed INF-389 to add a CI cancellation/cleanup hook that attempts a safe unlock or at least surfaces the lock ID so we can clean up faster. Also suggested adding a short TTL/cleanup job for stale locks (24h) — will add to the ticket.

alex_w: Thanks all. I'll add a blurb to the oncall docs: if apply crashes, check DynamoDB locks and confirm runner is dead before force-unlock. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
